picks.what: The Alcázar above the Eresma, engraving in Alexandre de Laborde’s Voyage pittoresque et historique de l’Espagne
picks.why: the Alcázar on its rock before the 1862 fire; already cropped to the image, high resolution

picks.file: Ansicht von Segovia mit der großen römischen Wasserleitung (SM 6780z).png
picks.what: General view with the Roman aqueduct, pencil drawing (Städel Museum)
picks.why: dated 28 August 1857; aqueduct, cathedral and old town all recognizable; very high resolution
color; cathedral tower above the town, the Alcázar at right and the Vera Cruz church below
old town and cathedral with the snowy Guadarrama behind; high resolution

notes: #3 (Joli) is Madrid’s Puente de Segovia, not Segovia. #1 is a larger photo of a Wyngaerde 1562 view from the north but badly stained and tinted; #2 was preferred for clarity. #5 date: Laborde’s plates appeared 1806–20 (the Cádiz pick used 1812 for tomo II; harmonize if wanted). P4: the 1890s photochrom of the Alcázar (#7) is a strong color alternative to the 1857 drawing but is under 40 years later, so only one was used. Salvany’s 1915 stereo plates (#14–#16) are low-resolution pairs.
